predecessors.name: Ottoman Empire
predecessors.text: Ottoman Palestine west of the Jordan, run by the Occupied Enemy Territory Administration until the civil administration of July 1920

successors.name: State of Israel
successors.text: Israel 'expand[ed] to encompass about 78% of the territory of the former British Mandate' (Mandatory Palestine page)

successors.name: Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan
successors.text: the West Bank, 'Transjordan seizing and subsequently annexing the West Bank'

successors.name: All-Palestine Government
successors.text: the Gaza Strip, 'the Kingdom of Egypt seizing the Gaza Strip' which 'established' the All-Palestine Protectorate

ledger.x: July 1920: a British civilian administration under a High Commissioner takes over Palestine.
7 March 1923: the Franco-British frontier is settled.
ledger.cpn: French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon

ledger.x: 14/15 May 1948: Israel takes most of the Mandate.
May 1948: Transjordan takes the West Bank.
May 1948: Egypt takes the Gaza Strip.

wars.name: 1948 Palestine war
wars.outcome: The civil war phase began on 30 November 1947 after the UN partition resolution of 29 November (33 to 13, 10 abstentions); the Mandate ended at midnight 14/15 May 1948 and 'the surrounding Arab armies invaded Palestine' the next morning.

certainty.note: The northern frontier was the 23 December 1920 convention line with a joint commission still to mark it; the 'Sea of Galilee' crossing and the Golan were disputed until 1923; the Transjordan limit was settled only on 16 September 1922.

Frontier fixed by the Paulet-Newcombe line of 7 March 1923 in the north and the Order-in-Council line 'up the centre of the Wady Araba, Dead Sea and River Jordan to its junction with the River Yarmuk' in the east; the Sinai/Negev frontier…
